answer: To resist sybils in an agent economy, each agent must lock a minimum stake in a time-locked vault for several epochs. An attacker spawning many identities pays a linear capital cost for every extra vault, making large-scale sybil farms economically unviable. Over time honest agents cultivate a reputation garden that boosts their reward share, while an occasional comet-style surprise audit randomly re-validates the vault ownership to catch recycled identities.
